samples.summary: `sectPrLengthPx` treats the literal attribute value "0" as absent, so the new `allowZero` branch is dead for the one case it exists for
samples.evidence: `const raw = el.getAttributeNS(W, name) || el.getAttribute(`w:${name}`); if (!raw) return undefined;` — the string "0" is falsy in JS, so `<w:pgMar w:top="0" .../>` returns `undefined` and the caller keeps its 96 px default. The function's own docstring says "a margin of 0 is a legitimate edge-to-edge layout" and adds `allowZero` (`px >= 0`) specifically to permit it, but that branch can never be reached for the literal `0` twips value that DOCX actually writes. Result: a Word document with zero margins imports as 1-inch margins. (The `!raw` shape predates the change; the new parameter documents an intent the code does not implement.)

samples.summary: `URI_CHARS` rejects characters that occur in real-world URLs, silently dropping otherwise-valid links and images from Markdown export
samples.evidence: `const URI_CHARS = /^[A-Za-z0-9\-._~:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=%-￿]+$/;` omits `|`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `"` and backtick, which browsers and CommonMark accept in a destination (e.g. `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Roboto|Open+Sans`, or any URL carrying `{}` template segments). `isEmittableUrl` returns false for these, so `inlineToMarkdown` emits the bare text and `imageInline` emits `[image]` — the link/image is lost from the export with no diagnostic. Previously such hrefs were emitted intact.

samples.summary: Format-painter source fallback still reads the run immediately *before* the selection — the exact case the `+1` was added to prevent
samples.evidence: When `normalized.start.offset >= startLen` and no later block up to `endIdx` has text (e.g. the selection continues into a table block, whose `getBlockTextLength` is 0, or `endIdx === -1` because the end is inside a table cell), `formatSourcePosition` returns `{ blockId: normalized.start.blockId, offset: normalized.start.offset }`. `caretInlineStyle` then falls through to the start block's *last* run, i.e. the run just before the highlighted text — the misread the method's docstring says it exists to avoid. The user copies a format they did not highlight.

samples.summary: Page Setup dialog calls `editor.getPageSetup()` / `setPageSetup()` with no capability guard, unlike the format painter which the PR explicitly hardens
samples.evidence: `useEffect(() => { if (!open || !editor) return; const current = editor.getPageSetup(); ... })` — the same PR adds `supportsPainter()` in `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:141` precisely because the frontend has no `tsc`, every `EditorAPI` double is `as unknown as EditorAPI`, and `EditorAPI` is exported for out-of-tree adapters. An editor lacking `getPageSetup` throws `TypeError: editor.getPageSetup is not a function` from inside the effect the moment the dialog opens, unmounting the document screen — the same blast radius the painter guard was written to avoid. `PageSetupButton` only checks `!editor`.

samples.summary: `assertUsablePageSetup` does not validate `orientation` or `paperSize.name`, so `writePageSetup` can still store something other than what it accepted
samples.evidence: The docstring promises "Everything this accepts, the resolver returns untouched", but the assert never inspects `setup.orientation` or `setup.paperSize.name`, while `resolvePageSetup` normalises any non-'landscape' orientation to `'portrait'` (types.ts:836) and substitutes `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP.paperSize.name` for a missing name (types.ts:832). A caller passing a malformed orientation gets a silent substitution rather than the promised `RangeError`.

samples.summary: `fitMargins` proportional scaling can leave a content box marginally below `MIN_CONTENT_PX` due to floating-point rounding
samples.evidence: `const scale = Math.max(0, (extent - MIN_CONTENT_PX) / total); return [near * scale, far * scale];` — `near*scale + far*scale` is not exactly `extent - MIN_CONTENT_PX` in IEEE-754 (e.g. extent 816, near/far 500/500 → sum can exceed 815 by ~1e-13), so the resolved content box can be fractionally under the 1 px floor the function is written to guarantee. Still positive, so layout survives; only the stated invariant is off.
